current.text: He is a rookie guard on Sacramento. He was one of the Kings' two first-round picks in the 2026 draft.
He is the backup point guard. Malik Monk is ahead of him on the depth chart.
He beat expectations in Summer League with 2.6 steals, 14 points and 94% FT in 26 minutes. He looked better than Sacramento's other first-round pick.
Experts call him a name to watch as a high-steals backup point guard. One expert says he could give useful stretches the way Keon Ellis did.
He is ranked 40th in one expert's dynasty rookie rankings, up from 42nd.
The Kings are expected to be one of the worst teams in the NBA. Their rotations are hard to predict.
Experts expect Sacramento to give rookies minutes.
Sacramento refused to play Malik Monk last season. Experts do not trust Monk's role in the rotation.
The Kings play 4, 4 and 3 games in our playoff weeks 19 to 21, so 11 games in total. They have 14 back-to-backs this season.

note: Yahoo gives him a value of 0 USD and ranks him 700th. ESPN does not rank him, and no one in our league drafted him last season, so he will not go in our 144-player auction. Watch him on waivers early in the season. Steals are his selling point, and he could get real minutes if Sacramento keeps sidelining Malik Monk or gives its rookies minutes as experts expect.
